source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A post-op client has religious food requirements. What shows cultural consideration?
options: Ask about and honor food customs
Tell family to stop bringing food
questions.rationale: Spiritual and cultural consideration means learning and maintaining the client's familiar customs to support healing.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1048 (PDF p. 1322)
questions.quote: Spiritual and cultural consideration reflects attempts to maintain familiar customs

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: How should the nurse address an older client from an unfamiliar culture?
questions.rationale: Using the formal name shows respect to older clients of any background; personal conversation not related to care is limited at first.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1049 (PDF p. 1324)
questions.quote: it is generally prudent to show respect for an older client of any ethnic background by using his or her formal name.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client speaks only a dialect the nurse doesn't know, and no interpreter is free. What is BEST before a dressing change?
questions.rationale: The ideal is a dialect-specific interpreter designated by the agency; family should not interpret medical information.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1051 (PDF p. 1327)
questions.quote: it is ideal for the nurse to call on a dialect-specific interpreter designated by the health care agency

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which factor belongs in a cultural and spiritual assessment?
questions.rationale: Cultural assessment covers nutrition, communication, high-risk behaviors, health practices, family roles, and spirituality.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1052 (PDF p. 1328)
questions.quote: nutrition, communication, high-risk behaviors, health care practices, family roles and organiz

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which food should be AVOIDED for a client on a kosher diet?
questions.rationale: Kosher diets avoid pork, meat of carnivores, and fish without scales or fins.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1055 (PDF p. 1333)
questions.quote: Clients who follow a kosher diet avoid meat from carnivores, pork products, and fish without scales or fins.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A woman with headache has long red welts on her back from coin rubbing. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: The nurse asks about home remedies and assesses cultural health practices; coin rubbing is a traditional remedy.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1057 (PDF p. 1335)
questions.quote: The nurse should ask the client if she has used any home remedies.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which death practice should the nurse expect for a dying Muslim client?
questions.rationale: Muslims desire the body to face Mecca. Hindus favor cremation within 24 hours.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1058 (PDF p. 1337)
questions.quote: Those of the Muslim faith desire their body to be facing Mecca.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A Muslim woman is stabilized after an assault. Which assignment is MOST appropriate?
questions.rationale: Gender roles influence care; many Muslim women should be cared for by a female nurse.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1059 (PDF p. 1339)
questions.quote: Information about family and gender roles will greatly influence the nurse’s plan of care.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which factor contributes to health disparities?
questions.rationale: Disparities arise from age, ethnicity, education, provider attitudes, geography, income, occupation, and health literacy.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1060 (PDF p. 1340)
questions.quote: Many factors contribute to health disparities

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Besides food and illness beliefs, what else should the nurse consider in nutrition care across cultures?
questions.rationale: Dietary preferences, food beliefs, and cultural perception of body size must be considered.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1061 (PDF p. 1341)
questions.quote: client perception of body weight and size relative to culture must

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which statement shows a client treated for TB understands discharge teaching?
questions.rationale: Close contacts must be tested and treated if positive. Drugs are completed; dishes need no special handling.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1063 (PDF p. 1343)
questions.quote: Any close contacts with the client must be tested and treated

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on home IV antibiotics should report which finding early?
questions.rationale: Pain, drainage, and edema signal site infection; early detection prevents septicemia.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1064 (PDF p. 1346)
questions.quote: The nurse instructs the client to report clinical indicators of an IV site infection, including pain, drainage, and edema

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which statement shows understanding of home fire safety?
options: 'Smoke alarms and quick exit save lives.'
questions.rationale: Early smoke detection and immediate evacuation reduce deaths, since alarms sound before flames appear.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1068 (PDF p. 1350)
questions.quote: The early detection of smoke using a smoke detector and immediate evacuation from the house have significant and positive effects on mortality rates.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which statement on a low-sodium diet needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Frozen and processed foods are often high in sodium.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1070 (PDF p. 1352)
questions.quote: Sodium retains fluid, which leads to hypertension as a result of increased fluid volume.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which statement shows a pregnant woman understands toxoplasmosis prevention?
questions.rationale: Infected cats shed toxoplasma in feces; pregnant women avoid litter boxes and undercooked meat.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1072 (PDF p. 1354)
questions.quote: Infected house cats transmit toxoplasmosis through the feces.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which diet does a child with cystic fibrosis need?
questions.rationale: CF is managed with high-calorie, high-protein food plus pancreatic enzymes and fat-soluble vitamins. Fat is not restricted.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1073 (PDF p. 1355)
questions.quote: Children with CF are managed with a high-calorie, high-protein diet.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which measure relieves itching under a plaster cast?
options: Push a stick in with help
Blow cool air with a hair dryer
questions.rationale: Nothing is put inside a cast, and water weakens plaster. Cool air from a hair dryer can relieve itching.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1075 (PDF p. 1357)
questions.quote: Objects should not be put inside a cast because of the risk of scratching the skin

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is MOST important to determine before an arteriogram with contrast?
questions.rationale: Iodine or seafood allergy predicts dye reaction, and consent is needed for the invasive injection.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1097 (PDF p. 1381)
questions.quote: Allergy to iodine or seafood is associated with allergy to the radiopaque dye

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An older resident returns after several GI tests. Which assessment is the PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: GI tests need bowel prep and NPO status, so older adults risk dehydration and poor nutrition.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1100 (PDF p. 1384)
questions.quote: require that the GI tract be cleaned (usually with laxatives and enemas) before testing.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which sign fits dehydration from long-term diuretic use?
questions.rationale: Fluid deficit causes rapid pulse, weight loss, poor turgor, low output, and concentrated urine with high specific gravity.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1107 (PDF p. 1391)
questions.quote: concentrated urine with increased specific grav

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Allen's test checks collateral circulation of which artery?
questions.rationale: Before radial puncture, Allen's test confirms adequate ulnar circulation to prevent hand ischemia.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1114 (PDF p. 1398)
questions.quote: Allen’s test is performed to determine adequate ulnar circulation.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: ABG: pH 7.34, PCO2 37, HCO3 19. Which imbalance is present?
questions.rationale: pH below 7.35 with HCO3 below 22 and normal PCO2 is metabolic acidosis.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1116 (PDF p. 1400)
questions.quote: Metabolic acidosis occurs when the pH falls to less than 7.35 and the bicarbonate level falls to less than 22 mEq/L

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the priority after an intravenous pyelogram?
questions.rationale: Fluids help clear the dye. Activity is as tolerated.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1134 (PDF p. 1419)
questions.quote: After IVP, the client should take in increased fluids to aid in the clearance of the dye

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which IV solution is isotonic?
questions.rationale: D5W is isotonic in the bag, as are 0.9% NaCl and lactated Ringer's.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1146 (PDF p. 1433)
questions.quote: Five percent dextrose in water is an isotonic solution

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What maintains the integrity of an ABG sample?
questions.rationale: ABGs use a heparinized syringe, placed on ice and sent immediately. No preservative.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1155 (PDF p. 1442)
questions.quote: The sample of blood is placed on ice and sent to the laboratory immediately.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which care is correct after a bone biopsy?
questions.rationale: The site is monitored for swelling, bleeding, or hematoma; VS every 4 hours for 24 hours; the site is elevated.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1199 (PDF p. 1491)
questions.quote: Nursing care after bone biopsy includes monitoring the site for swelling, bleeding, or hematoma formation.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the PRIORITY before an arthrogram with contrast?
questions.rationale: Because of contrast allergy risk, the nurse first assesses allergy to iodine or shellfish.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1200 (PDF p. 1492)
questions.quote: Because of the risk of allergy to contrast medium, the nurse places the highest priority on assessing whether the client has an allergy

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After laryngectomy, oral intake starts with which food type?
questions.rationale: Oral intake begins with semisolids; liquids are added once semisolids are managed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1214 (PDF p. 1507)
questions.quote: Oral intake after laryngectomy is started with semisolid foods.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which order should wait until a comatose client is intubated?
questions.rationale: Intubation must precede gastric feeding to prevent aspiration.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1273 (PDF p. 1574)
questions.quote: Intubation should always precede gastric feeding to prevent pulmonary aspiration.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client says he goes to PT, but the record shows two missed visits. Which response uses confrontation?
options: 'I see you missed the last two visits.'
questions.rationale: Confrontation presents the facts from the record to address avoidance.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1281 (PDF p. 1582)
questions.quote: the nurse employs the therapeutic communication technique of confrontation.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A head-injured client keeps pulling his feeding tube. Which restraint is BEST?
questions.rationale: Mittens prevent pulling without resistance, which could raise ICP. Wrist restraints cause resistance.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1284 (PDF p. 1585)
questions.quote: Mitten restraints are useful for this client because the client cannot pull against them

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A family says their father started wandering at night and got out once. What should the nurse say FIRST?
options: 'Tell me more about when this began.'
questions.rationale: The nurse first assesses and collects data about the behavior change.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1288 (PDF p. 1589)
questions.quote: The nurse responds to the family by assessing the situation and collecting additional data

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: An older client asks the home nurse to buy her groceries. What is BEST?
questions.rationale: The nurse completes the assessment and then finds immediate and long-term solutions with the client.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1289 (PDF p. 1590)
questions.quote: the nurse’s first action is to finish the assessment and then find immediate and long-term solutions

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which belongs in seizure precautions?
questions.rationale: Suction is ready for secretions, and the client is accompanied during activities. Nothing goes in the mouth.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1291 (PDF p. 1592)
questions.quote: Suction equipment should be readily available to remove accumulated secretions after the seizure.
